method: Full pinned source read, Git/SHA256 verification; compiled original extracted text truncation loop with minimal state struct, no GLib or formatter substitution.
findings: Text length initially uses g_utf8_strlen but subsequent truncation iterates bytes. Original loop control for éé at max_len1 emits lone c3 byte, invalid UTF8. This proves loop behavior, not rendered terminal output.
Unicode scalar count also differs from terminal cell width for combining/wide glyphs; no wcwidth handling is present.

Matching percent divides bytes_remaining by bytes_after_preprocess without local zero guard; converting nonfinite percent to int in bar calculation is a source-level edge, not an executed full-scanner failure.

ETA averages actual read-byte deltas and elapsed monotonic time, adds4096 nominal bytes per remaining file and caches display using real wall clock. Filtering skipped bytes and file-overhead heuristic mean ETA is not throughput evidence.
ioctl terminal-width return is unchecked; state width may remain zero/stale. Text/bar widths are clamped nonnegative, but terminal resize refresh occurs only every250 callbacks.
On abort cursor is restored and callback returns before normal timer/means cleanup; total lifecycle/resource impact needs handler ownership validation. No leak claim established by source alone.
Timer pointer is not nulled after normal destruction in PRE_SHUTDOWN. Repeated lifecycle events require separate validation before claiming use-after-free.
INIT hides cursor regardless of output TTY and replay bypasses progress output. Summary state is ignored, so bar does not independently certify full scan success.

executed_control.scope: Original byte truncation loop compiled with a minimal state struct; no full formatter, GLib or terminal runtime.

limits: No full upstream runtime, visual terminal qualification or new speed measurement.
